# Zoloti Maky — Ukrainian Dance Ensemble, San Francisco

> Zoloti Maky (Zuh-loh-tee Mah-kee) is a San Francisco-based Ukrainian dance ensemble, named after California's Golden Poppy ("zoloti" means golden, "maky" means poppies). We perform traditional Ukrainian folk dances and original choreography at cultural festivals, community events, fundraisers and private celebrations across the San Francisco Bay Area and beyond. Zoloti Maky is a program of UACC (Ukrainian American Coordinating Council), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

## Booking and contact

- Email: zolotimaky@gmail.com
- Location: San Francisco, CA (performing across the Bay Area and beyond)
- Contact form: https://zolotimaky.org/#contact — subjects: performance booking, event collaboration, general inquiry, sponsorship / donation
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/zolotimaky/
- Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/zolotimakydanceensemble
- Performance formats: full programs, smaller-format pieces and duets, all-women or mixed programs, and choreography for specific occasions (Christmas performances, television broadcasts, weddings, community fundraisers). Short demonstrations or participatory elements are possible on request.

## Repertoire

- Pryvit (pree-VEE-it): traditional welcome dance, greeting the audience with bread and salt on an embroidered rushnyk; about hospitality, respect and community.
- Hopak (hoh-PAK): Ukraine's national dance, known for athleticism, rapid footwork and virtuosic jumps; rooted in Zaporizhzhian Cossack traditions; danced by women and men.
- Hutsulka (hoot-SOOL-kah): from southwestern Ukraine (Carpathian mountains), associated with weddings; fast, intricate footwork and a lively rhythm.
- Koketka (koh-KET-kah): playful folk-dance duet about a boy trying to win over a girl who is not easily impressed; acting, fast spins, danced by our soloists.
- Shchedryk (SHEH-dryk): our own choreography for the women of Zoloti Maky, danced with shawls to the melody of "Shchedryk" ("Carol of the Bells"); slow and graceful, a favorite at holiday shows.
- Devyatka (deh-VYAT-kah): playful folk dance for one man and two women, full of flirting, competition and humor.
